kept_sections: Introduction / issue statement (deficiency redacted; item amounts kept as inputs)
facts_from_discussion: Petitioner admits that he received $25 of interest income in 2015.
Petitioner admits that he had gambling winnings of $2,994 in 2015.
Petitioner contends he had gambling losses exceeding the winnings shown on the Forms W-2G, but he admitted he kept no records of his gambling activity; no amount of gambling losses was substantiated.
There is no evidence of any itemized deductions other than the claimed (unsubstantiated) gambling losses.

Petitioner testified that he arrived at the $6,500 IRA deduction roughly by doubling his $2,890 contribution to the Arizona State Retirement System, to account for the State's matching contribution and his own.

The $2,890 retirement contribution was made as a pretax reduction of petitioner's salary and was excluded from the wages reported on his Form W-2; the record shows no other retirement or IRA contribution for 2015.
notes: The court refers to the $2,890 state-retirement-system contribution as an 'IRA contribution'; carried over as the factual description (pretax salary reduction excluded from W-2 wages) without the court's deductibility conclusion.
